title: # I used Codex to track down a WebGL startup freeze in my mech tower defense game
author: MuscularHobbit
selftext:
I’m making MECH VS ZOMBIES in Godot. You fortify city buildings between waves, then pilot a mech to defend a hospital when the zombies arrive. I wanted the playtest to run on [itch.io](http://itch.io) so people could try it without downloading anything.



The browser build had an awkward problem: you’d click Start and the game would hang long enough to look broken. I used Codex to time different parts of startup instead of guessing what was slow. One thing we found was that the game was rebuilding the mesh that the fake searchlight falls on across the map. The light still needed to move, but the mesh didn’t need to be rebuilt every time. We saved it as an asset and compared the builds. On my Edge tests, median startup went from about 18 seconds to 11.



That’s been the most useful part of working with AI so far: I can report what feels wrong while playing, then ask Codex to help me measure it and test one change at a time.



The 10-wave browser playtest is here: [https://lordtony.itch.io/mech-vs-zombies](https://lordtony.itch.io/mech-vs-zombies) (keyboard and mouse).



If you try it, I’m especially curious about the first prep phase: could you tell what to fortify and why, or did you just hit Next Wave and see what happened?

comments.author: VesperQuest
comments.body: I'm really starting to believe the Dead Internet Theory is real.
